description: HAWQS is a web platform that builds and runs Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) watershed models for any part of the conterminous United States, from pre-loaded national input data (NHDPlus, PRISM, NEXRAD, Crop Data Layer, NLCD, SSURGO, National Wetlands Inventory, National Inventory of Dams, NASS and others). Users pick a catchment at HUC8, HUC10, HUC12 or HUC14 resolution, edit land use, fertiliser, urban, point source, conservation practice and climate change inputs as scenarios, run SWAT and compare daily, monthly or annual flows, sediment, nutrients, pathogens, BOD, dissolved oxygen, pesticides and water temperature in tables, charts and maps, then download project files for offline use. The US EPA Office of Water funds it and Texas A&M's Spatial Sciences Laboratory develops it; it is available free after registration, version 2.0 is in beta, and its citation record in the Texas Data Repository is CC0 with no files. Coverage is national for the lower 48 states. Caveats: version 2.0 is still labelled beta, and no source code for the platform is linked. Simulation uses: catchment scenarios of land use, climate and point sources for water-quality planning, drought and climate adaptation. Related records: SELDM (model-usgs-seldm-stochastic-empirical-loading-dilution) and the US National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams).
licence: Free web service; the citation record in the Texas Data Repository is CC0 1.0; SWAT itself is public domain
